##### Bipartite Random Network FFRCISTG

###### Bipartite graphs

A bipartite graph is one where nodes are partitioned into two classes and edges connect only across classes.  In random-interference problems, it is often useful to model people on one side and places or events on the other.   An edge then represents a person’s affiliation with a place, and interference arises because multiple people may be connected through the same location.  This structure allows us to represent exposures that are not purely person-to-person, but mediated by shared environments.

###### BRNFFRCISTG

A bipartite RNFFRCISTG is am RNFFRCISTG in which all graph generators produce bipartite graphs with the same partitioning.
